title: How to build a $10M ARR B2B AI agent startup: boring industries, small agents, systematic distribution
summary: Greg lays out a framework for a vertical B2B AI agent business: target "boring" industries run on Excel and email, build chains of small specialized agents instead of one giant one, and grow through a three-phase distribution playbook (organic content, paid amplification, webinars). He also covers funnel metrics, expansion paths and exit options.

principles.text: Target boring industries whose expensive human labor is stuck in spreadsheets, documents and email chains.
principles.quote: Look for industries still running on Excel and email.

principles.text: AI agents beat traditional SaaS because they adapt to how people already work instead of forcing new workflows.
principles.quote: AI agents flip this model. They adapt to how humans already work.

principles.text: Build small, specialized agents that each own one step; they are easier to sell, more reliable and more transparent.
principles.quote: Instead, build small, specialized agents that each handle one discrete part of a workflow:

principles.text: Start selling with one agent that solves an immediate pain point, then chain more agents onto it.
principles.quote: Easier to sell. You can start with one agent that solves an immediate pain point

principles.text: Products don't sell themselves; run a systematic distribution plan, starting with short problem-solving videos ending in a free lead magnet.
principles.quote: The biggest mistake AI startups make is expecting the product to sell itself. It won’t. You need a systematic approach to distribution.

principles.text: Once organic content shows what resonates, pour paid spend into the winners and keep shipping new lead magnets.
principles.quote: Pour ad spend into your highest-performing organic content
